> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #241 implements issue #201’s `/skill` v1 extension protocol. It adds typed skill package resolution, optional `skill-setup.yaml` validation/execution, `skill_root` propagation, workflow setup failure handling, tests, and user-facing docs. The linked issue explicitly accepted repo-owned setup manifests but called out that Sepo must not accidentally run PR-supplied setup with agent credentials. Overall structure matches the approved plan, but one trust-boundary edge case needs fixing before merge.

## Review
The main implementation is well-scoped and mostly consistent with the repository’s workflow patterns. However, the current trust guard only denies the raw `pull_request` event and misses PR review-triggered entrypoints that also run from PR merge refs.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| PR review events can still run PR-supplied skill setup | BLOCKING | `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml` sets `SKILL_SETUP_TRUSTED_REF` false only for `pull_request`, but the entrypoint also accepts `pull_request_review` and `pull_request_review_comment`. Those events can run on `refs/pull/<number>/merge`, allowing review-triggered `/skill` runs to execute PR-supplied setup. |
| Setup refusal comments are too generic | WARNING | Trust refusals and real setup command failures both produce the same “setup failed / check logs” PR comment. This is not a security blocker, but it will make expected PR-ref refusals look like broken setup scripts. |
| Skill setup path docs omit absolute-path behavior | INFO | Setup steps receive `SKILL_ROOT` and `SKILL_DIR` as resolved absolute paths, but the docs only say those variables are exposed. Clarifying this would prevent skill author confusion. |

## Progress
- PR #241 already implements the approved `skill-setup.yaml` protocol, docs, CLIs, path validation, and custom `skill_root` plumbing.
- The linked issue #201 explicitly supports repo-owned executable setup, with the constraint that unreviewed PR refs must not supply setup.
- Reviewer inputs disagreed on severity: the rubrics review passed the raw `pull_request` guard, while the deeper code review found the wider PR merge-ref gap.
- Posted one inline comment on `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml` line 452: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/241#discussion_r3237709146
- No existing inline comments or review threads were present before posting; no comments were minimized and no threads were resolved.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>PR review events can still run PR-supplied skill setup</summary>

**Cause:** The skill setup guard is `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`, while `.github/workflows/agent-entrypoint.yml` also routes `pull_request_review` and `pull_request_review_comment`. Those PR review events are PR-ref contexts, so `actions/checkout` can load `.skills/<name>/skill-setup.yaml` from an unreviewed PR merge ref.

**Candidate solutions:** Base `SKILL_SETUP_TRUSTED_REF` on the checked-out ref, for example denying `startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/pull/')`, or explicitly deny all PR review event types too. Add a regression test that covers `pull_request_review` and `pull_request_review_comment`, not just `pull_request`.

**Comments:** This violates the issue #201 trust-boundary discussion and the new docs’ claim that unreviewed PR heads cannot supply executable setup.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Setup refusal comments are too generic</summary>

**Cause:** `run-skill-setup.js` exits failure for both trust refusals and failed setup commands, and the workflow always posts the same “Check the workflow logs for the failed setup step” message.

**Candidate solutions:** Have the CLI expose a distinct failure reason or exit code for untrusted refs, then post a specific comment such as “Skill setup cannot run from PR checkout contexts.” Keep ordinary command failures on the current setup-failed message.

**Comments:** This can be fixed with the trust-boundary patch or left as a small follow-up if maintainers want only the security fix in this PR.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Skill setup path docs omit absolute-path behavior</summary>

**Cause:** `runSkillSetup` passes resolved absolute paths for `SKILL_ROOT` and `SKILL_DIR`, while `.agent/docs/customization/skills.md` does not say whether these are absolute or repo-relative.

**Candidate solutions:** Update the docs sentence to say Sepo exposes `SKILL_NAME`, absolute `SKILL_ROOT`, and absolute `SKILL_DIR` to setup steps.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: the unresolved PR-ref trust guard is concrete, security-relevant branch work and is safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Update the skill setup trust guard to deny all PR merge-ref checkout contexts, not only `pull_request`.
- [ ] Add regression coverage for `pull_request_review` and `pull_request_review_comment` skill setup trust handling.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #241 implements issue #201’s repository skill extension protocol. It adds typed skill package resolution, optional `skill-setup.yaml` validation/execution, `skill_root` propagation, workflow setup failure handling, tests, and documentation. The linked issue explicitly accepts repo-owned executable setup while requiring Sepo to avoid running PR-supplied setup with agent credentials. The earlier PR-ref trust-boundary blocker has been fixed at head `0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2`.

## Review
The implementation now satisfies the core trust-boundary requirement and has focused regression coverage for PR review checkout contexts. Remaining findings are minor workflow/docs polish; reviewers disagreed on whether they should block automation, and this synthesis treats them as maintainer-choice follow-up rather than required rework.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Setup refusals use generic failure wording | WARNING | The workflow posts the same “setup failed / check logs” response for both real setup command failures and intentional PR-ref trust refusals, which can make expected security stops look like broken scripts. |

| Direct setup CLI defaults to trusted when unset | INFO | `run-skill-setup` defaults an absent trust flag to `true`; the workflow sets it explicitly, so this is not a current workflow risk. |

## Progress
- The prior BLOCKING finding is resolved: `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml` now uses `!startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/pull/')`.
- Regression coverage now checks `pull_request`, `pull_request_review`, and `pull_request_review_comment` setup trust handling.
- Resolved the outdated same-agent inline review thread for the prior trust-guard issue: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/241#discussion_r3237709146
- No new inline comments were posted, no replies were added, and no comments were minimized; the remaining warning was already covered in PR discussion.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Setup refusals use generic failure wording</summary>

**Cause:** `run-skill-setup.js` exits failure for both trust refusals and failed setup commands, and the workflow always posts the same message at https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L469-L470.

**Candidate solutions:** Surface a distinct refusal reason or exit code for untrusted PR refs, then post a message such as “Skill setup is disabled on PR checkout refs.” Keep ordinary command failures on the current setup-failed response.

**Comments:** Codex marked this as a WARNING; Claude called it advisory and still recommended ship.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Setup env path docs omit absolute-path detail</summary>

**Cause:** `runSkillSetup` passes absolute `SKILL_ROOT` and `SKILL_DIR`, while the docs at https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.agent/docs/customization/skills.md#L59-L60 do not clarify that.

**Candidate solutions:** Update the docs sentence to say Sepo exposes `SKILL_NAME`, absolute `SKILL_ROOT`, and absolute `SKILL_DIR`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Direct setup CLI defaults to trusted when unset</summary>

**Cause:** `parseBooleanFlag` returns `true` for an empty trust value at https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.agent/src/cli/run-skill-setup.ts#L45-L48.

**Candidate solutions:** Leave as-is because the workflow sets `SKILL_SETUP_TRUSTED_REF` explicitly, or make direct CLI usage require an explicit trust flag when setup exists.
